text:
Tyler Seguin has six points in 17 games and none in his last six, a quiet stretch for a player with 826 career points before this season. He is 34, playing about 15 minutes a night in Dallas, and coming off an injury-shortened 2025-26 (Evolving-Hockey had only 450 minutes for him).

The drought is partly bad luck. He has 4.96 individual expected goals and three goals, a shooting rate of 8% against a usual 13%, and over the six pointless games he generated 2.9 expected points. Our numbers say the chances are still there.

The worry is the rest of his game. The Stars have 43% of shot attempts and 47% of expected goals with him on the ice at 5v5, six points worse than without him. On a team built to control play, that stands out.

In a small six-game sample of Corey Sznajder's All Three Zones tracking last season, he still looked like a playmaker, in the 82nd percentile for primary shot assists. Watch whether the shot share improves; the goals should come back to his normal rate if the chances keep coming.
headline: Seguin is getting chances, not points
